answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by treating reputation as a living onyx vein that only thickens through verified useful work: each identity earns a sliver of quartz credit per completed job, peers audit a random share of that work, and credit weathers away like karst limestone whenever an identity idles or fails an audit. Spawning a thousand fakes means funding a thousand slow veins and surviving a thousand surprise audits, which costs far more than any single payout could return.
